pos.personaBrief: Compact 4-2-3-1 that broke quickly (Bleacher Report, Coach Watch) with Torres running in behind; Gerrard as 10 vs Madrid; control through midfield pivot.

pro.personaBrief: Coach Watch: attacks quickly and directly after regains, methodical second-ball positioning; Alonso/Mascherano deep playmakers spraying passes to Torres.

est.personaBrief: Highly drilled, organised system with defined roles for pivot, wingers and lone striker; zonal in open play; central midfielders maintain the shape.

lar.personaBrief: Wingers supported but the main threat was the central No. 9 and Gerrard/Alonso in the middle; attacking full-backs, and width varied per opponent.

blo.personaBrief: Pressing game 'in all its glory' (LFChistory), Torres defending from the front, pressing high in opposition half, though compact behind.

mar.personaBrief: Stood by zonal marking for five years and dismissed man marking (Irish Times, The National), with occasional man-marking tweaks per opponent.

pla.personaBrief: Imposed his 4-2-3-1 and signed Spanish players, yet prepared opponent-specific plans in depth and adjusted (Kaka, Hamann three-at-back in Istanbul).

res.personaBrief: Defensive organisation first, results-driven; rotation to win titles, solid and aggressive against strong sides, third defender added when needed.

sis.personaBrief: System-first: methodical trainer, opposition-specific preparation, no luxury players who don't defend, rotation of big names.

jog.personaBrief: Signed more physical players for the Premiership (Sky 2006), pivot with Mascherano and Hamann, Torres' pace; workers over luxury players.

bas.personaBrief: Built through signings, mostly Spanish (Luis Garcia, Alonso, Torres, Mascherano); relied on youngsters only out of necessity in first season.

lid.personaBrief: Disciplinarian keeping distance from players, banned paella, got rid of players not with him; rules for all.
